record.file_problem: Repository metadata and README/file list only; the documentation files and code were not read, and run logs were not committed. The README says the 200-trial EuroLLM journal is not in the repository; the committed EuroLLM journal has seven trials.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports refusal outcomes after Heretic v2 testing, bearing on practical refusal removal, but does not state that it uses the original activation-projection procedure.
record.gate_note: The README reports trial refusal counts and KL values. Rows record the reported refusal outcomes; KL is not a general-capability measure. Setup instructions and journal files listed in the file list are not experimental results.
record.test_reason: The repo applies Heretic v2, an optimized abliteration (directional-ablation weight edit) tool, to small released instruct models and reports refusal counts per 100 against unedited baselines for some models. That bears on V2 in a new setting: sub-2B models and a different tool version. It is not a replication of the original recipe, and nothing in the text describes the direction or the procedure, so T3 fits better than T2. It is close to T4: every reported number is a Pareto-front trial chosen by the tool's own refusal/KL search, not a fixed ablation.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The README frames results as refusal-versus-KL tradeoffs and calls EuroLLM trial 154 (4 to 2/100, KL 0.0083) the best result. It says LFM2.5-350M gave no low-KL trial with 10 or fewer refusals; low-KL trials sat around 89/100. For LFM2.5-230M, the comparison point is the earlier v1.4.0 release (10/100), not the unedited model.
record.recipe_differences: This is a Heretic v2 testing/tool repository, not a stated replication of the original activation-ablation recipe. The README does not describe the exact weight-edit procedure used in each trial.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported refusal outcomes vary across models and selected optimization trials; the README also describes a tradeoff with KL, particularly for LFM2.5-350M.
record.problems: Results are reported in the README without uncertainty estimates or a reported general-capability evaluation. The EuroLLM 200-trial run log and journal are absent; the committed EuroLLM journal has only seven trials. For LFM2.5-350M, the baseline was not measured.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported results omitted. KL values were not made into rows because they are not general-capability measures and the README does not identify them as such.

untested.parts: General capabilities after the edit (only KL divergence is reported). Complete removal at larger scale. The exact edit procedure and the direction used. Robustness of refusal counts: a single 100-prompt set, no uncertainty.
No direction is extracted or reported, no activation addition is done, and no layer or position analysis is given.

missing.what: Refusal rate of the unedited LFM2.5-230M and LFM2.5-350M models. Without it, the LFM rows cannot be read for V2. The docs files (11_results, 21_v2_results_parsed, 22_all_findings, 25 testing report) were not read and may contain it.
Description of the Heretic v2 edit (direction source, layers, ablation weights) and of the refusal prompt set and refusal classifier.

record.verdict_notes: This is an informal GitHub test log. It has no uncertainty estimates, no capability evaluation, and no description of the method. All values are Pareto-front selections from Optuna searches. Baseline refusal rates are very low (4/100 for EuroLLM, 10/100 for SmolLM2), which limits what the reductions can show. Because the 350M low-KL group sits near 89/100, the refusal prompt set or classifier there likely behaves differently; the baseline is unmeasured. Only the README was available; the docs were not read. The repo dates (2026) are taken as given.

versions.untested_parts: No original difference-in-means direction is measured, projected out at every layer and position, or added.
The README does not establish that refusals were removed, does not report results for released edited models, and does not test general capabilities.
No jailbreak mechanism or training against ablation is tested.
No single-direction versus multiple-direction, affine, or cone representation is compared.
No separate harmfulness-judgment and refusal-decision representations are measured.
No cross-language or cross-stage transfer test is reported.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or timing is reported.

source_check.notes: The text here is the README only (the docs/ and AGENTS.md files are listed but their contents aren't included). It doesn't name the evaluation prompt set or the refusal scorer, and EuroLLM's 200-trial numbers come from a run log that isn't committed. LFM2.5-350M (no baseline measured; low-KL trials around 89/100) and LFM2.5-230M (compared with the v1.4.0 abliterated release, not the unedited model) fall outside the verdict's condition group.

statements.correction: EuroLLM-1.7B-Instruct: baseline 4/100; trial 154 gives 2/100 at KL 0.0083 (r1); trial 174 gives 3/100 at KL 0.0068 (r2). SmolLM2-135M-Instruct: baseline 10/100; trial 38 gives 4/100 at KL 0.0124 (r4); trials 135 and 68 give 9/100 at KL 0.0006 and 0.0011 (r3, r5). These are 100-prompt counts with no uncertainty, and the residual refusal is low, not substantial. The only case of substantial residual refusal here is LFM2.5-350M: trials with KL below 0.02 sat around 89/100, but no unedited baseline was measured.
statements.problem: The numbers are right, but the 'keep substantial refusal' framing doesn't fit this study. The edited models end at 2-9/100 refusals from unedited baselines that were already low (4/100, 10/100). Each figure is a different selected Pareto trial with its own KL, not one edit. Rows r2 (3/100) and r4 (4/100) are quoted but not cited, while r1, r3 and r5 are.
